sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by flow cytometry (PMC7116137, PMC12229354) and by endoglycosidase/immunoblot (PMC4513639); receptor trafficking to plasma membrane verified. Functional assays (e.g. ligand binding, cAMP) were not reported specifically for the tagged constructs in these studies.
sites.rationale: Three independent papers (PMC4513639, PMC7116137, PMC12229354) all report full-length, membrane-anchored human ADORA1 carrying a short epitope tag on the extracellular face. None names a specific residue. The raw topology string begins with 'O' (no signal peptide), so residues 1–9 are the extracellular N-terminus and the C-terminus (291–326) is intracellular. Because exactly one terminus is extracellular, the topology uniquely determines the insertion point: insert_after_residue = 0 (prepend before M1), residue_after = M (confirmed by reading seq[0] in Python). TM1 begins at residue 10, leaving 9 residues of extracellular linker between the tag and the membrane — sufficient clearance (≥3 aa). No signal peptide is present, so there is no risk of the tag being cleaved. The primary supporting quote is from PMC4513639 (explicit 'at the N terminus'); PMC7116137 ('N-terminal FLAG epitope') and PMC12229354 ('extracellular region', topology-derived to N-terminus) corroborate the same site. PMC4513639 reports N-terminally FLAG-epitope- and SF-TAP-tagged full-length human A1R stably expressed in HEK293 cells; glycosylation status and surface expression were verified by endoglycosidase treatment and immunoblot. PMC7116137 reports an N-terminal FLAG-epitope-tagged full-length human A1R whose surface delivery was confirmed by flow cytometry in transiently transfected HEK293 cells (wild-type and G279S mutant). PMC12229354 reports a Myc-tagged full-length human A1R whose cell-surface expression was confirmed by flow cytometry on CAR T cells. No paper names a specific residue; position is topology-derived: the C-terminus (291–326) is intracellular, so the N-terminus (residues 1–9, extracellular, no signal peptide) is the only extracellular terminus available. [validation: surface_only; position: topology_derived; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

sources.claim: In addition, we generated N-terminally modified versions by addition of either a FLAG epitope or a Strep-Tactin II-FLAG tandem affinity purification tag (SF-TAP) at the N terminus ( Gloeckner et al., 2007 ).

literature_notes: Ledger lines for eYFP/GFP fusions (PMC7116137 line 5; PMC4513639 lines 6, 8, 9) were not used: no insertion residue is named and for GPCRs these fusions are conventionally placed at the intracellular C-terminus, which is confirmed intracellular (291–326) by the topology landmarks. The YFP-tagged A1R-Y288A construct (PMC4513639) was also excluded: Y288 falls within TM7 (268–290) and is a point mutation, not a tag-insertion site; the YFP position is unspecified. The Myc-tag line from PMC12229354 ('extracellular region') resolves to the same N-terminal site by topology and does not add a second distinct site. All three qualifying ledger lines therefore converge on a single N-terminal prepend site, reported once at rank 1.
